title: Dynamic tenancy slicing and fair-bursting controls for Dedicated GPUs
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity report intermittent tail-latency and throughput drops when a small number of tenants burst large batch workloads. Current slab-based allocation and hard quotas either over-provision (waste) or cause hard rejections. Goal: introduce a dynamic slice model for physical GPU pools that guarantees baseline throughput per slice while allowing short-term fair bursting using credit buckets and soft-eviction. The feature must integrate with autoscaling policies so slices can expand/contract across machine boundaries, respect placement affinity (e.g., PCIe topology), and surface clear observability (per-tenant throughput, credit balance, eviction events). Constraints: - Must not require a separate hardware partition for each tenant. - Changes should be incremental and toggleable by config flags. - Keep latency SLOs for P0 customers and provide graceful degradation for best-effort tenants. Success metrics: - Reduce tail P95 token latency regressions caused by noisy neighbors by >= 80% in controlled experiments. - Maintain or improve average cluster GPU utilization by <= 5% reduction vs current baseline. - No production customer-facing errors introduced in canary for 72 hours.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline throughput guarantee enforced per configured slice (tokens/sec) and validated via perf harness
Credit-based bursting allows short spikes up to configurable burst_size without violating other slices' baseline
Soft-eviction preemption path implemented for best-effort jobs; preempted workloads resume automatically when credits recover
Autoscaler integrates: slice-scale-out triggers GPU rebalancing and preserves placement affinity
End-to-end observability in Console: per-slice throughput, credit balance, eviction history, and token-cost impact
Canary rollout demonstrates no increase in customer error rate and meets latency SLOs for a 72-hour window
implementation_plan: Design: finalize slice model and credit bucket math (this ticket)
Runtime: implement slice abstraction and admission controller (PR: runtime#4892)
Scheduler: extend placement plugin to consider slice membership and affinity groups
Autoscaler: add slice-level metrics and scaling policy hooks
Control plane: APIs to create/update slices, set baseline and burst parameters
Console: surface slice telemetry and controls in Dedicated UI
Integration tests: synthetic noisy neighbor scenarios and end-to-end canary
Rollout: internal dev cluster -> staging -> restricted canary -> ramp
decisions: Use credit-bucket model (leaky bucket) for burst accounting instead of token-window to simplify accounting across distributed schedulers
Soft-eviction (preempt with graceful resume) preferred over hard-kill to preserve customer work and reduce retries
Slices are logical constructs mapped to groups of allocations; we will avoid mandatory physical GPU pinning except for high-isolation reserved slices
Autoscaler will operate at slice granularity; scaling actions may move work between slices if policy allows
risks: Increased scheduling complexity could lead to higher placement latency for large-scale rebalances
Credit misconfiguration may either allow noisy neighbors or be too conservative and reduce utilization
Affinity constraints (NUMA/PCIe) may limit scale-out options and complicate autoscaling decisions
Rollback path must be robust in case of unforeseen regressions during canary
